name: Bhadora Industries Ltd
tagline: Small integrated LV power-cable and wire manufacturer (PVC / XLPE / Aerial Bunched cables for discoms, infra, EPC and government T&D) - Rs ~219 Cr microcap, revenue Rs 18.8 Cr (FY23) -> Rs 110.7 Cr (FY25) -> ~Rs 121 Cr (FY26), Q1 FY27 net sales +226% YoY to Rs 45.3 Cr on mix + realisations, but FY26 operating cash flow was Rs -27 Cr against Rs 10 Cr PAT as debtor days jumped to ~155 - a real cash-conversion warning
business_overview: Bhadora Industries (incorporated 1986, IPO'd 2024) manufactures low-voltage power cables and wires - having moved from PVC cables to XLPE and Aerial Bunched (AB) cables - for the infrastructure, EPC and government electricity-distribution (discom) segments, and is expanding toward value-added / specialised cables and an 'integrated' cable-manufacturing facility. Sovrenn Discovery seed (2026-09-02, 'Excellent Results Jun-26'). No dedicated ValuePickr thread - web/filings/news-only read. IPO (Aug-2025, NSE SME, Rs55.62cr raised) proceeds were earmarked to part-finance a new manufacturing facility at Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, plus working capital and general corporate purposes -- so the 'integrated facility' capex is partially IPO-funded, not wholly unfunded as this project's prior light-pass read suggested.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 219 Cr (Sep-2026, price ~Rs118); reported ROE ~19.3% (3yr avg ~34.4%), ROCE ~23.6%; debt-to-equity ~0.29 (lower than the ~0.9 this project's prior light pass had estimated)
FY23 Rs18.8cr -> FY25 Rs110.7cr -> FY26 ~Rs121cr (PAT ~Rs9.96-10cr, down slightly YoY despite revenue growth)
FY26 PAT ~Rs10cr vs FY25 Rs10.8cr -- profit essentially flat/slightly down even as revenue grew, i.e. margin compression
Net sales Rs45.32cr vs Rs13.92cr (+226% YoY) -- management attributes it to improved product mix, higher realisations and broad end-user demand, not a disclosed order book
FY26 operating cash flow was Rs -27cr against Rs10cr PAT; debtor days jumped from 72 (FY25) to ~155 (FY26); working-capital days from 36 to ~150
New integrated manufacturing facility at Khargone, MP, part-financed by Aug-2025 IPO proceeds (Rs55.62cr raised) alongside working capital and general corporate purposes
fundamentals_narrative: Bhadora is a genuine microcap growth spike -- revenue roughly 6x'd from FY23 to FY25 and Q1 FY27 net sales are up 226% YoY -- but the deep-dive pass surfaced a materially worse cash-conversion picture than the prior light pass captured: FY26 operating cash flow was Rs -27cr against Rs10cr reported PAT, debtor days jumped from 72 to ~155 days and working-capital days from 36 to ~150 in a single year, and FY26 PAT was flat-to-down YoY (~Rs10cr vs Rs10.8cr) even as revenue grew -- i.e. the P&L growth did not carry through to cash or even to the bottom line on a full-year basis. Two things also correct the prior pass's estimates: debt-to-equity is actually ~0.29 (not ~0.9), and the 'integrated facility' capex is partially funded by the Aug-2025 IPO's Rs55.62cr proceeds (not wholly unfunded), though the disclosed IPO allocation does not appear to size-match the scope management now describes. Promoter holding has also risen (62.75% -> 65.59%), not fallen -- there is no promoter-exit signal here. The core bear case stands: this is a small, commoditised LV-cable maker against far larger players, the +226% quarter is realisation/mix-led rather than confirmed volume, and it remains genuinely thin on independent scrutiny (no VP thread, no analyst coverage, no disclosed order book).

four_box.note: Discom/grid T&D capex + electrification-metals demand is a real sector tailwind; +226% quarter is realisation/mix-led not confirmed volume growth, FY26 PAT was flat-to-down YoY and operating cash flow went to Rs-27cr -- tam weak; explicitly commoditised LV-cable segment vs much larger players (Polycab, KEI, RR Kabel) -- moat no; ~22x P/E already prices continued fast growth against a genuinely deteriorating cash-conversion picture -- valuation weak.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~22x trailing earnings on ~Rs10cr FY26 PAT prices continued fast growth; for a commoditised copper-pass-through LV-cable maker a ~12-15x exit is fair, so ~30-40% EPS CAGR is needed for 2-3 years to justify today's price
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue growth could stay high on discom/grid T&D demand if the Q1 FY27 +226% is volume-backed, but management credits mix + realisations; PAT growth is now a real open question after FY26 PAT came in flat-to-down YoY despite revenue growth, and working-capital/interest drag could compress it further
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: depends on the Khargone facility executing on its partially-IPO-funded capex and on order-backed volume replacing realisation-led gains, plus a resolution of the FY26 cash-conversion problem
market_expectation.gap_basis: a ~22x multiple prices durable high growth, but the +226% quarter is realisation/mix-led (reversible in a copper pass-through), FY26 operating cash flow was Rs -27cr against Rs10cr PAT, debtor days jumped to ~155, FY26 PAT was flat-to-down YoY, and the segment is crowded with far larger players
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

track_record.note: Per screener.in (FY23-FY26): revenue growth >14% and ROCE >20% held in FY23-FY25, but FY26 breaks the pattern -- PAT was flat-to-down YoY (~Rs10cr vs Rs10.8cr) even as revenue grew, and operating cash flow turned sharply negative (Rs -27cr) on a working-capital blowout (debtor days 72->155). This is a tiny-base IPO ramp (revenue ~Rs15cr FY22 -> ~Rs121cr FY26); the high historical ROCE is a small-base artefact and FY26 is the first year the pattern has cracked.

deep_dive.conviction_update: Low-Medium -> Low. The deep dive corrected two things in Bhadora's favour (debt-to-equity ~0.29 not ~0.9; capex partially IPO-funded not unfunded; promoter holding rising not falling), but surfaced a materially worse cash-conversion and full-year-profit picture than the prior light pass had: FY26 operating cash flow of Rs -27cr against Rs10cr PAT, debtor days 72->155, and PAT flat-to-down YoY despite revenue growth. On balance the newly-confirmed cash-flow and earnings-quality problems outweigh the corrections, so conviction moves down to Low.
